annotation.method: Codex read the complete 55-page local paper, surveyed every section, algorithm, labeled theorem, lemma, corollary, appendix result, discussion, conclusion, and reference, visually checked all selected source pages, searched all 24 frozen mounted object modules, and compiled private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P16 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published open-access journal version; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis 46(4), 2026, printed pages 1939-1993

rejected_candidates.candidate: floating-point notation, gamma definition, condition numbers, singular values, and the forward-error definition in Section 2
rejected_candidates.reason: These are definitions or recalled standard tools. T1 instead selects the complete displayed normwise backward-error minimum identity.
They are assumptions of the framework rather than proved conclusions.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 3.1 full MOD-GMRES attainable forward/backward error theorem
rejected_candidates.reason: It is the central unrestarted result, but a source-faithful formalization would require singular-value optimization, key-dimension existence, least-squares backward stability, and the complete Paige-et-al. residual argument absent from the frozen baseline. Lemma 4.2 preserves the paper's reusable generic iterative-refinement recurrence without pretending those delegated ingredients are formalized.

Its modular coefficients depend on every operation model and on Theorem 3.1. The selected T2 isolates its generic one-step backward-error clause, and T3 captures the resulting mixed-precision restart convergence.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems 5.1-5.3 for HH-GMRES, MGS-GMRES, and FGMRES
rejected_candidates.reason: These compatibility results depend substantially on external Householder/MGS/Paige analyses. They are less novel than the Section 6 applications and would duplicate the same final residual shape.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems 6.1 and 6.2 for simpler GMRES and CGS2-GMRES
rejected_candidates.reason: Both are viable but require separate QR/Arnoldi/Gram-Schmidt execution contracts and singular-value rank arguments. Theorem 6.3 is the paper's mixed-precision application and directly tests whether high- and low-precision operation models can be composed into actual forward- and backward-error guarantees.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems A.1, B.1, C.1, C.3, Lemma C.2, and Corollary C.4
rejected_candidates.reason: The appendices contain important supporting results, but they would require full finite QR/CGS2 implementations or polar/singular-value infrastructure. They are subordinate to the selected main-text progression.

rejected_candidates.candidate: prospective discussions of deflated, randomized, and block GMRES and all literature comparisons
rejected_candidates.reason: These are research directions, comparisons, or engineering guidance rather than completed universally quantified results of this paper.

T1.decision: Use the complete unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum and normalized-residual identity on printed page 1942, under the standing nonsingular-system and nonzero-right-hand-side assumptions from printed page 1939.

T2.decision: Retain the backward-error half of Lemma 4.2 as a project-corrected task: make the proof-required but unstated iterate comparison explicit, retain exact identity (4.18), model lesssim with an O(scale^2) remainder, and derive recurrence (4.15) from (4.1), (4.2), and (4.14). The corrected task is excluded from ordinary faithfulness scoring.

T3.decision: Use Theorem 6.3's fixed-run actual-error contraction for a fully stored mixed-precision restarted MGS-GMRES execution: retain the high-precision residual/update models, operational low-precision MGS-Arnoldi correction and residual initialization, restart-dependent key dimensions, columnwise least-squares model, actual inverse, dimension-only c(n,k_i), and both attainable floors; formalize the first-order displays by exact affine inequalities without an unprinted stationary denominator.

selection_policy: Use results proved in this paper and exact consequences of their displayed hypotheses, not empirical or prospective discussions.
Expose the paper's Euclidean/Frobenius normwise structure with finite-dimensional paper-scoped definitions.

For fixed-run first-order claims, either retain a source-supported higher-order semantics or state an exact strengthening explicitly; do not invent fixed-precision remainder certificates or stationary factors absent from the selected result, and keep every restart-dependent quantity and key dimension explicit.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only from the 24 modules in metadata/library_olean.json.
